outcome.technical: guard-uncommitted.py: when the sibling parser cannot tokenize a line, reading() now builds executed_text(command), a quote- and heredoc-aware walk. It drops quoted-delimiter heredoc bodies, including one inside a command substitution inside double quotes (the house description form), and drops quoted ARGUMENTS. It keeps every command substitution and backquote, inside double quotes and inside unquoted-delimiter bodies too. It keeps a quoted program word and every quoted argument of git. It truncates at a quote or substitution that never closes; bash runs nothing past one, verified with bash -c on an unterminated quote, which ran only the earlier complete lines. It returns None, keeping the raw-line reading and the unchanged widest refusal, when any command in the line can run text it is handed: a shell, eval, make, xargs or exec, a program named by path, or an interpreter not running a script file. That judgement uses the shared _config.program_candidates, is_shell, is_interpreter and runs_own_program. The view is re-parsed with the sibling's git_invocations and judged on the operation; that reading is labelled 'executed', and its refusal says the line could not be tokenized and what was read. If the view will not parse either, the shapes grade the view. Also fixed: the pre-filter's tree-wide dot (_DOT) now ends where a shell word ends, so a variable assigned from a substitution running a tree-wide checkout is no longer waved through before the parser is asked; it was allowed on HEAD, tokenizable or not. gu41 is reworded to assert the 'could not be tokenized' basis: its old 'TEXT' assertion now belongs to the raw path, and gu51 pins the two labels apart. New cases gu43-gu51. Selftest 52/52. Gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py` exit 0 (1/1 files ok, 52 cases). Mutation probe: <scratchpad>/p153-3/probe/mutations.py, output in output.txt beside it, run as `python3 mutations.py <checkout>`. Baseline 52/52, and all nine rows were KILLED, including both over-fire directions (M8 every interpreter a runner turned gu44 and gu49 red; M9 every command a runner did the same) and the defect restored (M1 turned gu44 and gu49 red). Only that task's files are open here.' The probe therefore lives in the scratchpad. (b) The first submit call was refused by the live plugin guard-history-rewrite, whose message opens: '[guard-history-rewrite] `git st` + `ash` moves work between the working tree and the stash' (spelled split here for the same reason). The return object's prose quoted the stash command, and because the heredoc head names its script by a QUOTED path, _config._plain_script_run does not vouch for it, so the body was graded as code and fell to the raw-text arm. (c) The second submit was refused for absolute machine paths; this filing writes <home>/ and <scratchpad>/. Apart from those spellings, the content is unchanged. The names targets, judge, parser and decide found in guard-release.py, require-claim-block.py, the skills and CHANGELOG are those files' own same-named symbols: .claude hooks do not import this file, and none of this file's signatures changed, so they are still correct. FOUND, OUT OF SCOPE (not edited; not a declared file): the root of the tokenized-path half is _config._head_runs_body in plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py. Its _HEAD_INDIRECTION search matches the command substitution that ENCLOSES the cat heredoc, so every house-form body (commit message or description) is graded as SHELL by every guard sharing split_heredocs. Measured: git_invocations on an audit-task add whose house-form description has a body line opening with the stash verb returns a stash invocation with args ['is','banned','here']. A body line opening with a tree-wide checkout would be refused by this guard on the tokenized path, and the plugin's history guard reads the same bodies as commands; refusal (b) above is a second instance of the class. The fix belongs in _config: read the head from the innermost open substitution, and stop letting a quoted script path disqualify a plain script run. It needs a register entry and its own task.
outcome.descriptive: guard-uncommitted no longer refuses a command for heredoc bodies or quoted arguments that only quote destructive git, while every real destructive command stays refused, including one inside a command substitution that the pre-filter used to miss.
